title_en: Guo Dexian — aggravated punishment for escaping during labor reform and committing another crime
keywords_en: Criminal; Theft; Escape; First Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Handling Escapees or Repeat Offenders among Prisoners and Persons Subject to Re-education through Labor; Aggravated Punishment for Escape from Prison and Commission of New Crimes; Combined Punishment for Multiple Crimes; Supporting Plaintiff; Escape from Prison during Sentence; Multiple Thefts; Floating Crime
full_text_en:
Guo Dexian — Aggravated Punishment for Escape and Crimes During Labor Reform

The criminal offender Guo Dexian, male, 34 years old, native of Liangshan County, Shandong Province. In 1977, he was subjected to two years of reeducation through labor for theft. In December 1980, he was sentenced to eight years of fixed-term imprisonment by the Luwan District People's Court of Shanghai for habitual theft. He was then serving his sentence at the Shanghai Second Labor Reform Management Team.

During his sentence, on the morning of September 14, 1981, Guo Dexian, together with fellow inmate Wu Yimin (separately handled), took advantage of outdoor labor to escape. On the evening of September 15, he was apprehended at Nanjing Railway Station and returned to the labor reform facility. On October 19 of the same year, Guo Dexian, together with fellow inmates Huang Minxuan and Yao Yongfa (both separately handled), sawed through the iron bars of the cell door with a hacksaw blade, dug through the cell roof, and climbed over the prison wall to escape. After escaping, Guo Dexian successively fled to the Guesthouse of Yixing County, Jiangsu Province; the North Station Hotel in Shanghai; the First Guesthouse of Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province; the Zhongzhou Hotel in Zhengzhou City, Henan Province; and the Taohualin Hotel in Yichang City, Hubei Province, where he stole cash totaling RMB 587 from travelers, 87 jin (1 jin = 0.5 kg) of grain coupons, one electronic calculator, one camera, one semiconductor radio, as well as clothing, cigarettes, cloth coupons, military passes, letters of introduction, and other items. On the afternoon of November 29 of the same year, Guo Dexian entered the Guesthouse of Luoyang Bearing Factory in Luoyang City, Henan Province, and stole a semiconductor radio belonging to a traveler surnamed Lu. He was caught by the public and handed over to the public security authorities, again being returned to the labor reform facility. In the early morning of March 1, 1982, Guo Dexian, together with fellow inmates Li Yun, Chen Libin (both separately handled), and Hu Xinmin (at large), removed iron pipes from bed frames, pried open the cell roof, and climbed over the wall to escape. After escaping, Guo Dexian successively fled to the Second Guesthouse of Wuxi County, Jiangsu Province, and the Government Guesthouse of Zhucheng County, Shandong Province, where he stole cash totaling RMB 340 from travelers, over 50 jin of grain coupons, as well as cigarettes, letters of introduction, and other items. At noon on September 23 of the same year, Guo Dexian sneaked into the Branch of the International Travel Service of Zibo City, Shandong Province, and stole cash totaling RMB 630 and grain coupons from persons including Cheng × × and Liu × ×. He was caught by the public and handed over to the public security authorities, where he was brought to justice.

In January 1985, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court accepted the case. After trial and determination, the court found that the criminal offender Guo Dexian had escaped three times during his sentence, twice damaging prison facilities, thereby committing the crime of escape under Article 161 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. After escaping, Guo Dexian successively fled to six provinces and municipalities, accumulating a total period of eight months, and committed nine thefts, with the amount stolen totaling nearly RMB 2,000. He was truly incorrigible and committed the crime of habitual theft under Article 152 of the Criminal Law. Moreover, because he escaped and committed crimes again during labor reform, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Handling Escapes or Repeated Crimes by Persons Undergoing Reform through Labor or Reeducation through Labor, the punishment should be aggravated. Guo Dexian, after being sentenced and before the completion of the execution of his sentence, committed the crime of escape and the crime of habitual theft, two crimes. In accordance with Articles 66 and 64 of the Criminal Law, he should be subject to combined punishment for multiple crimes. Guo Dexian's habitual theft seriously disrupted social order, and in accordance with Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. The property stolen by Guo Dexian, in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, should be recovered.

On March 12, 1985, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court, by aggravated punishment, sentenced Guo Dexian to fifteen years of fixed-term imprisonment for habitual theft, with deprivation of political rights for five years; to five years of fixed-term imprisonment for escape; plus the remaining sentence of six years, one month, and fourteen days from the previous crime, totaling twenty-six years, one month, and fourteen days. The combined sentence was decided to be twenty years of fixed-term imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for five years. The court ordered recovery of Guo Dexian's illicit gains: RMB 1,557 in cash, 137 jin of grain coupons, one electronic calculator, and one camera.

On June 5, 1985, the 226th meeting of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 11 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, and in summarizing trial experience, considered that the judgment of the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court in this case reflected the spirit of imposing heavier and aggravated punishment according to law on criminals who resist reform during labor reform, escape, and commit crimes again.
